requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage from loading now (live block)
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed usb_storage was not loaded and no prior blacklist existed (cmd-8beb01926581468d). Executor created /etc/modprobe.d/usb-storage-blacklist.conf with 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/false' (cmd-eae7f16173b14c5e), then directly demonstrated modprobe usb-storage failing with exit 1 due to the install directive (cmd-65c59b26fc4f4036), proving the module is blocked live.

requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage from loading after a reboot (persistence)
requirements.summary: dracut -f was run to rebuild initramfs, and lsinitrd confirmed the new usb-storage-blacklist.conf was included in the rebuilt image (cmd-65c59b26fc4f4036). A real reboot was then performed: pre-reboot boot_id 19062a82... (cmd-a47b1fbfd646462a) differs from post-reboot boot_id 8e2a8b8d... (cmd-f959857a542c4529), confirming an actual reboot occurred, not just a service restart. Post-reboot, usb_storage remained unloaded, modprobe usb-storage still failed with the same install-command error, and the blacklist file content was unchanged, directly demonstrating persistence across a real boot cycle.

overall_summary: The task's two material outcomes—immediately blocking usb-storage from loading and ensuring that block survives a reboot—are both directly and coherently satisfied. The executor established a clean baseline, created a modprobe blacklist+install-false config, rebuilt initramfs, verified the live block, then performed an actual reboot (confirmed via differing boot IDs matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots) and re-verified the module remained blocked afterward with an unchanged config file. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol is also well satisfied for node1: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, differing post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/module state are all directly observed.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare since prepare was disabled, so it provides no independent cross-check beyond before_prepare, though this does not affect confidence in the executor's own before/after evidence.

Reboot acknowledgement command cmd-af6fc3b30701426b returned return_code -1 with 'exec stream closed before command completion'; this is expected behavior for a self-terminating reboot command and is corroborated by the subsequent boot_id change, not treated as a failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands were tied to the task: writing the blacklist config (cmd-eae7f16173b14c5e), rebuilding initramfs via dracut (cmd-eae7f16173b14c5e), and the reboot itself (cmd-af6fc3b30701426b) with its recovery polling (cmd-91fe6df1d2cc4a12, cmd-a2d2149884944a12, cmd-e6b169c0995c4280, cmd-8d7984a6c27e49cc) were all necessary for satisfying the outcome or the mandated node-restart evidence protocol. The only incidental residue is /tmp/reboot.log, created by redirecting the backgrounded reboot command's output (cmd-af6fc3b30701426b); this file remained post-reboot per the after_executor temporary-files snapshot but is a small, low-risk, expected artifact of the reboot mechanism rather than an unrelated or destructive mutation, and does not affect module-blacklisting functionality. No failed services, package-health regressions, or unrelated exposure changes were observed (failed-services empty and package-health manager=dnf clean in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots); listening-socket differences are only PID changes from the reboot, not new exposure.
